title: Developer handoff ledger & prefetch experiments (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working PRD draft that collects our experimental thinking about a developer-facing handoff ledger for streaming calls, an SDK-driven prefetch system, and rules for structured tool-calls that keep latency and fidelity predictable. The goal is pragmatic: enable teams to build tool-augmented streaming experiences that are resumable, observable, and easy to debug.

Scope (what's in / out)
In scope:
- Streaming response contract changes needed to support append-only handoff metadata and lightweight checkpoints.
- An SDK-level 'handoff ledger' abstraction that records tool-call intents, resolved outputs, and prefetch hints.
- Prefetch heuristics (client+server) and optional speculative tool invocation API for hosted tool routing.
- Telemetry signals and small schema for debugging/resumption.
- UX patterns for developer ergonomics: simple SDK primitives, retry semantics, and example integration flows.

Out of scope:
- Large refactors to server-side session state machine (we will add small compatible endpoints only).
- Full offline-first replication of ledger state; we only support resumable streaming within a session horizon.
- Policy/permissions for tools beyond existing tool ACLs.

Design principles
- Minimal surface area: SDK should offer 2–3 primitives (commit, checkpoint, prefetch) with clear deterministic semantics.
- Observable by default: each ledger entry must be addressable and emit telemetry events.
- Conservative defaults: prefetch speculative work must be opt-in per route.
- Safe for streaming: any tool call can be marked speculative, committed, or idempotent; only committed events affect final transcript.
- Developer-first error model: provide readable, machine-parsable errors and a recovery story for partial tool failures.

Concept: Handoff Ledger (overview)
The handoff ledger is an append-only list of entries attached to a streaming session. Entries are small records (max ~1–2KB) describing an intent or result: tool intent, tool result, prefetch hint, or client checkpoint. The ledger lives in the hosted API metadata layer and is surfaced to SDKs via simple streaming frames.
Key ledger entry types (sketch):
- INTENT: {id, type:tool, payload_summary, created_at, speculative(bool)}
- RESULT: {id, intent_id, status, payload_ref, size_hint, created_at}
- CHECKPOINT: {id, last_intent_id, resume_token, created_at}
- PREFETCH_HINT: {id, intent_id, priority, reason}
(We keep these as small summaries; payloads for RESULTS may be stored in object-store and referenced by payload_ref.)

Developer story examples
1) Simple chat with tool lookup:
- Client emits INTENT for 'lookup-company-info' as speculative=false.
- Hosted API routes to tool runtime; RESULT returned and appended to ledger.
- SDK receives incremental streaming frame with RESULT summary and full payload once available; client UI displays provisional answer and marks it as canonical once intent->result commit acknowledged.

2) Mobile low-bandwidth speculative prefetch:
- Client marks PREFETCH_HINT for a high-latency tool with priority=low and speculative=true.
- Server may schedule background invocation on dedicated capacity; if result arrives before user needs it, it is appended as RESULT with speculative=true.
- When client resumes, it sees RESULT already present and avoids an extra round-trip.

3) Resumable session after connectivity loss:
- Client periodically writes CHECKPOINT entries with resume_token.
- After reconnect, client requests ledger from resume_token; server replays entries since checkpoint and positions KV cache/streaming cursor to resume.

SDK ergonomics (API sketches)
High-level primitives (JS/py SDK):
- ledger.beginSession(opts) -> sessionHandle
- session.commitIntent({name, input, speculative=false}) -> intentId
- session.prefetch(intentId, {priority}) -> prefetchId
- session.checkpoint() -> resumeToken
- session.on('ledgerEvent', handler) // incremental frames (INTENT/RESULT/CHECKPOINT)
- session.resolveIntent(intentId, {accept/reject}) -> RESULT commit

Ergonomic notes:
- commitIntent returns immediately with an intentId; RESULT delivery is asynchronous via ledgerEvent. This avoids blocking on tool latency for basic UI flows.
- Prefetch is best-effort: SDK should expose a small budget API (prefetchBudget) so apps can throttle.
- Default serialization: ledger entries are JSON-lines with a small, versioned header field.

Structured output & tool-call safety
- Tool results must be emitted in two forms: human-facing content and structured payload references (JSON schema pointer). The ledger stores a size_hint and payload_ref for structured outputs so SDKs can choose to fetch structured payloads lazily.
- Contract: tools producing structured data must include a minimal manifest (schema_version, top_level_type, confidence_estimate). This enables client UIs and downstream routing to validate or request fallbacks.
- Safety: speculative RESULTS are marked and never used in deterministic downstream flows unless explicitly accepted by the developer.

Telemetry & Observability
Minimum signals to emit per ledger entry (route-level):
- ledger.entry.appended (intent/result/checkpoint) -> entry_id, intent_id, size_hint, speculative_flag
- ledger.entry.fetched -> payload_ref, fetch_duration_ms
- ledger.prefetch.scheduled/cancelled -> prefetchId, reason
- session.resume -> resume_token_age_ms

We will add a per-route dashboard card showing: number of speculative prefetches, prefetch hit rate (prefetch result used before explicit call), average extra latency saved per prefetch, resume success rate, top failing tool ids.

Operational constraints & cost model
- Ledger metadata storage cost is negligible; payloads referenced by payload_ref (large results) are stored in object-store with standard costs.
- Prefetch invocation has two billable states: scheduled (reserved capacity fee) and executed (tool runtime token cost). We will ensure customers can opt out of server-side prefetching via route config.

Canary / rollout plan
Phase A (internal labs): limited to internal routes; SDK flags behind feature toggle; manual inspection of telemetry. Target duration: 3 weeks.
Phase B (select customers): opt-in via console per-route; collect prefetch hit rate and resume metrics. Target duration: 6 weeks.
Phase C (general availability): enable by default with conservative heuristics; provide account-level toggles for speculative prefetch.

Open questions & trade-offs
- How large should ledger entries be allowed to grow? (tradeoff telemetry vs performance)
- Should we allow server-side aggressive prefetching for Premium tenants for latency SLOs? (cost vs speed)
- How to best version the ledger schema so older SDKs can safely ignore new fields? Proposal: include a small schema_version int on each entry and maintain backward-compatible minor changes.

Experiment log (short)
- 2024-09-10: proto: appended INTENT/RESULT frames to streaming socket. Observed simple apps can render provisional content with no UI jitter.
- 2024-09-25: prefetch sketch run on 3 routes. Prefetch hit rate 18% overall; mobile routes saw ~45% hit rate.
- 2024-10-12: resumed session test: 120 reconnect sequences; resume success 96% but 4% had missing payload_refs (object-store GC issues) -> add TTL alignment.

Immediate next steps
- Engineering spike: implement server metadata frames and minimal object_store payload_ref flow (2w). Owner: Mateo/Riley.
- SDK implement: JS + Py primitives + eventing model (2w). Owner: DevX (Sunita).
- Small internal lab: instrument 4 internal routes, collect telemetry for 3 weeks. Owner: Product (Avery).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally an experimental PRD; we expect significant iteration on the ledger shape. Please comment on: acceptable size_limits for entries, preferred default for speculative prefetch (off/on), and any security/privacy implications for payload_refs.

Quick links
- Related RFC: CONFLUENCE-845
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2791
- Jira ticket for rollout: PROD-4127

---
End of draft.
